The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS score: 8.1) and codenamed SSHole (or *sshole), impacts Linux systems that run OpenSSH on the musl C library with Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) disabled
control_implications.focus: OpenSSH on the musl C library with Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) disabled
control_implications.headline: OpenSSH on the musl C library with Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) disabled exposes passwordless sign-in
control_implications.significance: This vulnerability allows unauthenticated root access on affected Linux systems, weakening vulnerability management controls that rely on timely patching. The vulnerability and asset owners should confirm whether any systems run OpenSSH on musl libc with PAM disabled and verify remediation status.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: A fix for CVE-2026-83844, a remote code execution flaw in Windows Paint, is now in the Microsoft Store. Paint gets this fix only through a Store update, not through Windows updates. The fixed build, 11.2609.401.0, was the newest Paint build in all ten countries The Hacker News checked today.
control_implications.focus: Microsoft Paint RCE fix now available but Windows Update won't deliver it
control_implications.headline: Microsoft Paint RCE fix now available but Windows Update won't deliver it extends patch deployment gap
control_implications.significance: The patch delivery mechanism bypasses standard Windows Update, creating a gap in change management validation. Change and service owners should verify that Store updates are included in patch approval workflows and that the fixed build is deployed across endpoints.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Two flaws in Barracuda's Email Security Gateway, an email-filtering appliance, can be chained to run commands on it as root, its highest level of access, with no login required. The company released patches on Monday, and the security firm watchTowr detailed the attack chain on Thursday.
control_implications.headline: Barracuda Email Security Gateway enables root access without login via chained flaws
control_implications.significance: An unauthenticated attacker can achieve root access on the email gateway, compromising a critical third-party security control. Supplier risk owners should confirm patch deployment on all Barracuda appliances and request assurance evidence from the vendor.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Passwords and API keys that developers typed into commands they approved in Claude Code are sitting in public GitHub repositories, where anyone can read them. When a user selects "Yes, and don't ask again," Anthropic's AI coding assistant can save the command, word-for-word, including the secret, in a project settings file.
control_implications.headline: Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' file exposes passwords and keys in public repositories
control_implications.significance: Developer secrets are being inadvertently committed to public repositories via an AI assistant feature, bypassing data protection controls. Data and privacy owners should audit code repositories for exposed credentials and implement secret scanning with automated revocation.

paragraphs.text: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in widely used infrastructure components are being actively exploited within hours of disclosure, including an OpenSSH authentication bypass on musl libc systems, a chained root access flaw in Barracuda Email Security Gateway, and an SSL-VPN MFA bypass in SonicWall firewalls. These events weaken vulnerability management and access management controls by demonstrating that patching delays and authentication gaps can be rapidly weaponized. Control owners should prioritize asset identification for affected OpenSSH, Barracuda, and SonicWall deployments and verify that emergency patching procedures are executed.

Control assurance gaps also extend to patch delivery mechanisms, third-party service providers, and AI-assisted development workflows. A Microsoft Paint remote code execution fix is only available via the Microsoft Store, bypassing standard Windows Update channels; a French bank lost $133 million through a compromised service provider; and an AI coding assistant feature exposed over a thousand sets of credentials in public repositories. These findings highlight the need for change management to validate alternative patch sources, third-party risk programs to assess supplier access to financial systems, and data protection controls to scan for secrets leaked through AI tools.
